title: Catalog list pagination API decision
purpose: Document the unresolved choice between two Catalog API drafts for listing items and the pagination behavior the UI must support, so a human can select the authoritative contract.

scope.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string. UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects Catalog API draft A, a client can retrieve a catalog page as a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when a client sends GET /v1/items, then the response body is a JSON object.
Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when a client sends GET /v1/items, then the response body contains an items array.
Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when a client sends GET /v1/items, then the response body contains a next_cursor string.

stories.text: If a human selects Catalog API draft A, a user can move from the current catalog page to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when the response contains a next_cursor value for the current page, then the interface provides a control to move to the next page.

Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when the user activates the control to move to the next page, then the interface issues a follow-up GET /v1/items request that advances past the current page as specified by the selected draft A contract.

stories.text: If a human selects Catalog API draft B, a client can retrieve a catalog page as a top-level JSON array using page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected Catalog API draft B, when a client sends GET /v1/items with page and page_size query parameters, then the response body is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected Catalog API draft B, when a client sends GET /v1/items, then the request accepts page and page_size query parameters.

edge_cases.text: Requesting a next_cursor value that the selected contract does not recognize is a proposed error-handling case that the selected draft does not define.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: Selecting Catalog API draft A would leave the top-level JSON array plus page and page_size request unmet; selecting Catalog API draft B would leave the items array with next_cursor response unmet.

success_metrics.text: Proposed verification: inspect a GET /v1/items response against whichever draft a human selects and confirm the response shape and parameters match that selected contract.

open_questions: Which Catalog API draft should a human select as the authoritative contract, draft A or draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
Does the UI requirement to move to the next page also apply if Catalog API draft B is selected, and if so how is next-page navigation expressed under draft B?
